brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L gap to Mars Plastics' price and tighten payment to 30 days to free up ₹10.63 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics' price on the 30 ml HDPE bottle and 28 mm PP cap — our two biggest items.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.38/NOS for the 30 ml bottle (we pay ₹1.65/NOS today) and ₹0.81/NOS for the 28 mm cap (we pay ₹0.90/NOS today); together that saves us ₹15.97 L a year.
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics already supplies us these exact items at those prices, so we know they're real and we know Premier can hit them. The market openly asks ₹0.55–1.20/pc for a 28 mm induction-wad cap — typical is ₹0.85–0.95/pc — so ₹0.81 sits in the fair band and the market says there's headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. Right now we're handing Premier ₹16.09 L a year more than we pay our cheapest supplier for the same sort of goods.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹10.63 L cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight cash is for them. That means our plan leans on what we do know: Mars Plastics charges less for the same parts, the open market confirms there's room, and we have five strong alternates lined up — including Manjushree (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue) and three listed firms. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend gives us real weight, and the fact that we already buy these items cheaper elsewhere proves the price is achievable. Push firmly on price and payment — we have the data and the backup options to walk if they won't move.

evidence.point: We pay Premier ₹16.09 L a year more than our best price for rigid plastic packaging
Mars Plastics charges us ₹1.38/NOS for the 30 ml HDPE bottle; Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS — a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L a year
Mars Plastics charges us ₹0.81/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap; Premier charges ₹0.90/NOS — an 11.1% gap costing us ₹4.23 L a year
The open market asks ₹0.55–1.20/pc for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap, with typical pricing ₹0.85–0.95/pc; the verdict is market-fair with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
Moving payment from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L cash for us
Our annual spend with Premier is ₹1.29 Cr

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — with ₹2569.83 Cr revenue and a B health score (65/100); top second-source candidate already approved for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed firm with broad moulded and blow-moulded capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we can't see if they're stable or stretched — qualify Manjushree and one of the listed alternates now so we have a live second source before pushing too hard.
If they refuse the Mars price, be ready to shift volume immediately — waiting weakens our hand and costs us ₹16.09 L a year.
The 30 ml bottle gap (19.6%, ₹11.74 L/yr) is the big prize; don't let them trade the cap concession for nothing on the bottle.

We have six market backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) — all flagged medium confidence — but these are raw leads to qualify (verify capability and get quotes) before treating them as real options.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹16.09 lakh a year more than Mars Plastics charges us for the same bottles and caps — let's close that gap today.
